item.title: How bitcoin and gold went from a slump to an MVP week in just a few days
item.summary: # How bitcoin and gold went from a slump to an MVP week in just a few days - Click here to listen to this article - Share via - Bitcoin and gold snapped back from steep midyear slumps, with bitcoin vaulting above $77,000 and gold nearing $4,700 as investors rushed into alternative assets this week. - An aggressive Treasury move to double long-term bond buybacks, record U.S. debt and fresh inflation worries sparked a dollar sell-off and revived the global ‘debasement trade’ in hard assets. - In Washington, Trump’s push for crypto-friendly legislation and regulatory relief, combined with a massive short squeeze, amplified bitcoin’s surge and underscored its growing role alongside gold as a policy hedge. Bitcoin and gold shot higher this week, with both getting a boost from some frantic action surrounding the bond market, and the cryptocurrency also benefiting from activity in Washington. Bitcoin had dropped from a January high around $95,000 to below $60,000 at the end of June. Investors shied away from speculative assets earlier in the year, and crypto supporters were concerned about the lack of movement on proposed regulation of the industry. On Friday, bitcoin rose above $77,000.
